01.credentials

MEDIUM2▾

Vulnerability description

Credentials re-persisted via SharedPreferences.Editor (plaintext round-trip)

Remediation

Never log credentials, auth tokens, device identifiers, location or other sensitive values. Strip sensitive fields before logging, use release-time log stripping, and ensure logs do not leak PII (CWE-532: insertion of sensitive information into log files).

CWE · References

CWE-532Log Info Disclosure — developer.android.com ↗

02.code-exec

CRITICAL3▾

Vulnerability description

Attacker-marshalled Parcel (createFromParcel/readFromParcel unmarshal) reaches Class.forName / reflective instantiation — a malicious app crafts the Parcelable payload the victim app reflectively materializes

Remediation

Treat shared/external storage as untrusted: do not load executable or plugin code from it, verify APK integrity before any dynamic load, and scope read/write access with scoped-storage APIs rather than broad legacy permissions.

CWE · References

CWE-427Android Arbitrary Code Execution Via Third Party Package Contexts — oversecured.com ↗

03.provider

MEDIUM1▾

Vulnerability description

The attacker-supplied content:// URI of an exported provider is converted into a file path and opened (file theft via provider, e.g. ParcelFileDescriptor.open(uri.getLastPathSegment()))

Remediation

If a content provider is exported, validate every incoming URI against an allow-list, enforce per-path read/write permissions, and canonicalize paths before opening files to prevent traversal-based access to arbitrary app files.

CWE · References

CWE-22Path Traversal — developer.android.com ↗

04.ui-input

HIGH2▾

Vulnerability description

Text from an editable UI field reaches a network operation

Remediation

Treat user-typed input as tainted end-to-end: sanitize or allow-list it before embedding into URLs, WebView loads, SQL, or network requests, and never relay raw typed input into privileged APIs.

05.webview

HIGH1▾

Vulnerability description

Attacker-controlled content is loaded into a WebView with JavaScript enabled — the page can execute attacker-controlled scripts (Unsafe WebView URL navigation)

Remediation

Do not load attacker-controlled URLs or content into a WebView. Restrict loadUrl/postUrl inputs to an allow-list of trusted origins, disable JavaScript and file access (setAllowFileAccess, setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs, setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs) unless strictly required, and avoid exposing @JavascriptInterface bridges to untrusted content.

CWE · References

CWE-79Android Security Checklist Webview — oversecured.com ↗

06.network

HIGH3▾

Vulnerability description

A deeplink-supplied address reaches an internet service (Retrofit @Url, OkHttp, URLConnection, Socket) — forcing the app to connect to an attacker-chosen server (internet service address substitution / fake HTTP request)

Remediation

Send sensitive data only over TLS to trusted, allow-listed endpoints. Validate certificates (do not ship permissive TrustManager/HostnameManager implementations), avoid embedding personal or device identifiers in arbitrary URLs, and keep cleartext traffic disabled (networkSecurityConfig).

CWE · References

CWE-918Server Side Request Forgery — owasp.org ↗

07.activity-result

MEDIUM1▾

Vulnerability description

Deeplink-supplied data reaches setResult(data) in an exported activity — the result is delivered to the launching component

Remediation

When an exported activity calls setResult, treat the result as attacker-influenced: calling components receive data an external app may have shaped. Do not place secrets or privileged actions behind result flows, and validate any Intent returned as the result.

CWE · References

CWE-940Result — developer.android.com ↗

Instances

  • MEDIUMDeeplink data returned via setResult from exported activity❯

08.file

MEDIUM4▾

Vulnerability description

Intent-driven path traversal → an attacker-controlled path reaches a file create/write operation (File.createNewFile/mkdir/mkdirs, OutputStream/Writer.write, ContentResolver.openOutputStream, FileOutputStream/FileWriter, IOUtils stream-copy destinations)

Remediation

Canonicalize and validate every externally-influenced path before file access (File.getCanonicalPath + prefix check against a trusted base directory). Reject traversal sequences, use app-internal storage for sensitive files, and never delete or overwrite files outside the intended directory based on untrusted names.

CWE · References

CWE-22Path Traversal — developer.android.com ↗

09.redirection

HIGH1▾

Vulnerability description

Intent redirection — an attacker-controlled Intent is forwarded to startActivity/startService/sendBroadcast or another dispatch API

Remediation

Validate any externally-supplied Intent or URI before dispatching it. Prefer explicit component addressing (setPackage/setClass), reject or sanitize embedded intents, and never forward attacker-controlled extras into privileged dispatch APIs. Restrict exported components to the minimum surface the feature requires.

CWE · References

CWE-940Interception Of Android Implicit Intents — oversecured.com ↗

Vulnerability description

A path derived from an external-storage directory File reaches a file read/access operation

11.deserialization

MEDIUM1▾

Vulnerability description

Attacker-marshalled Parcel content reaches Gson.fromJson / Jackson.readValue — the unmarshaler materializes attacker-chosen types from IPC data

Remediation

Never deserialize attacker-controlled data with polymorphic type resolution enabled. Pin the target type (concrete classes, no Object/Serializable targets), avoid enableDefaultTyping/activateDefaultTyping with permissive validators, validate the input against a strict schema before parsing, and keep deserialization libraries patched against known gadget chains.

CWE · References

CWE-502Deserialization Cheat Sheet.html — cheatsheetseries.owasp.org ↗
